title: The Geargoyle That Quartered Itself
story: In the bell-crypt beneath the clocktower, Tremordyne the Quartering Geargoyle guards a stairwell full of frightened choir children. Every time a blade strikes it, the stone gargoyle splits into 4 smaller geargoyles — each one splitting again on the next strike. Mr 6 stops mid-swing and does the arithmetic instead, because the crypt only fits 300 geargoyles before the ceiling gives way.
question: Starting with 1 geargoyle, how many geargoyles would there be after 4 strikes?
solution: Each strike multiplies the count by 4: 1 strike gives 4, 2 strikes give 16.
Keep going: 3 strikes give 16 x 4 = 64, and 4 strikes give 64 x 4 = 256.
There would be 256 geargoyles after 4 strikes.
praise: Multiplying by 4 over and over was exactly the right idea — it just needed one more round of quadrupling to reach the fourth strike.
hint: Write the count after each strike in a little chain: 1, then 4, then... multiply by 4 each time and stop at strike four.
victory: Mr 6 sheathed his sword and announced the number 256 out loud; Tremordyne, who hated crowds, shuddered once and squeezed itself back into a single grumpy doorstop. The choir children tiptoed out singing.
imagePrompt: A numeral-six knight lowering his sword thoughtfully in a torchlit bell-crypt as a cracked stone gargoyle with clockwork gears trembles on the verge of splitting into four, frightened children peeking from the stairwell.
